method.vl_execution: prebuilt .wasm via `vl run <file.wasm>`; compile time measured separately
method.note: OTHER WORK MAY HAVE BEEN ON THE MACHINE — treat as PRELIMINARY.

void.reason: ADVERSARIAL AUDIT: cross-language ratio is unusable. The Rust column measures NOTHING — min-of-7 pinned wall time is 4.6ms, BELOW the 6.8ms empty-Rust-program startup baseline. deno reads 56.0ms (34% launcher) and python3 71.5ms (17% launcher); VL reads 1730ms. No REPS value fixes this: work is linear in REPS for Rust/JS/Py but VL is O(n^2) in N and linear in REPS, so REPS x20 puts Rust at ~92ms (still under the 200ms floor) and VL at ~34s. The VL-INTERNAL finding survives and should still be reported: doubling N multiplies VL by ~3.5x (O(n^2)) while Rust/JS/Python stay ~1.6-1.9x (O(n)) — VL's `s = s + c` reallocates and copies both operands every append. Do not publish any Rust/JS/Python-vs-VL multiple from this directory.

benchmarks.name: binarytrees
benchmarks.axis: realistic whole program: allocation + GC pressure (millions of short-lived 2-field nodes, plus one long-lived tree)

benchmarks.name: dispatch-table
benchmarks.axis: function values called indirectly: a 4-way dispatch table, as an if/else chain, as an array of function values, and as a function-valued struct field

benchmarks.name: lambda-hot
benchmarks.axis: closures: the per-call cost of a lambda in a hot loop, in four spellings (hand-inlined / named direct call / non-capturing lambda value / capturing closure)

benchmarks.name: mandelbrot
benchmarks.axis: realistic whole program: f64 arithmetic in a tight escape loop + integer bit packing into an array row buffer

benchmarks.name: map-filter-reduce
benchmarks.axis: higher-order functions: a callback-heavy map/filter/reduce pipeline over a 20M-element array, in three spellings (builtin methods / hand-written loops building the same intermediates / one fused loop)

benchmarks.name: nbody
benchmarks.axis: realistic whole program: f64 arithmetic over an array of mutable structs (O(n^2) pairwise force loop over 5 bodies)

benchmarks.name: spectralnorm
benchmarks.axis: realistic whole program: f64 array indexing in a tight O(n^2) inner loop, plus a small leaf function (A(i,j)) called once per element

benchmarks.name: bitcount
benchmarks.axis: popcnt / clz / ctz

benchmarks.name: bitops
benchmarks.axis: shift / and / or / xor / rotate

benchmarks.name: convert
benchmarks.axis: i32 <-> f64 conversion round trip

benchmarks.name: f64-accum
benchmarks.axis: f64 add/mul — accumulate + globals-cliff probe

benchmarks.name: floatops
benchmarks.axis: sqrt / abs / floor / min / max (no transcendentals)

benchmarks.name: i32-accum
benchmarks.axis: i32 add (wrapping) — trivial accumulate

benchmarks.name: i64-accum
benchmarks.axis: i64 add — trivial accumulate + globals-cliff probe

benchmarks.name: intdivmod
benchmarks.axis: i32 divide + remainder by a loop-varying divisor

benchmarks.name: mixed-width
benchmarks.axis: i32 + i64 + f64 in one loop, explicit `as` casts

benchmarks.name: binsearch
benchmarks.axis: binary search over a large sorted array — latency-bound unpredictable access plus one data-dependent branch per probe

benchmarks.name: fill-sum
benchmarks.axis: hot-loop element write + read on a pre-allocated i32 array; per-access bounds-check cost

benchmarks.name: matmul
benchmarks.axis: 2D matrix multiply over flat row-major arrays — cache behaviour on a 3-deep loop nest plus the per-access bounds check on the innermost read/modify/write

benchmarks.name: push-growth
benchmarks.axis: growth by push — geometric-reallocation amortization plus the push fast path

benchmarks.name: reverse-inplace
benchmarks.axis: in-place reverse — two cursors walking toward each other; 2 bounds-checked reads + 2 bounds-checked writes per iteration with no arithmetic to hide them behind

benchmarks.name: sort-heap
benchmarks.axis: sort — HAND-WRITTEN heapsort, the same algorithm in all four; branchy, cache-hostile random access over a large array

benchmarks.name: struct-aos
benchmarks.axis: array-of-structs traversal — read 2 of 4 i32 fields from every record; the A side of the AoS/SoA layout A/B

benchmarks.name: struct-soa
benchmarks.axis: struct-of-arrays traversal — the same records held as 4 parallel scalar arrays; the B side of the AoS/SoA layout A/B

benchmarks.name: map-i32
benchmarks.axis: i32-keyed hash map: insert, hit/miss lookup, iterate (VL's dedicated mono key rep)

benchmarks.name: map-string
benchmarks.axis: string-keyed hash map: insert, hit/miss lookup, iterate

benchmarks.name: set-ops
benchmarks.axis: hash set: build two overlapping string sets, then intersection / difference by membership test

benchmarks.name: struct-alloc
benchmarks.axis: GC pressure — allocating and discarding many short-lived heap structs (binary-trees shape)

benchmarks.name: struct-array-scan
benchmarks.axis: array of structs scanned by field — memory layout (inline records vs array of references)

benchmarks.name: struct-field
benchmarks.axis: struct field read/write in a tight loop — flat, then two levels of nesting

benchmarks.name: word-freq
benchmarks.axis: mixed map + string: tokenize a synthetic corpus and count word frequencies (read-modify-write upsert)

benchmarks.name: ackermann
benchmarks.axis: Ackermann — the densest call-overhead stress available: nested recursive calls in argument position, nothing memoizable or strength-reducible
benchmarks.python_scale_why: 558.6M vs ~21.8M calls; DEPTH also differs 8190 vs 510

benchmarks.name: deeprec
benchmarks.axis: deep LINEAR NON-TAIL recursion (5_000 live frames per call) — stack depth + return-path cost
benchmarks.python_scale_why: meta audit: BOTH depth and repeats change; no scalar factor is valid

benchmarks.name: fib
benchmarks.axis: naive binary (non-tail) recursion — raw call/return overhead with a near-empty body

benchmarks.name: flatcall
benchmarks.axis: static direct call to a tiny leaf function, 1.2e9 times — the CALL half of the call-vs-inline pair

benchmarks.name: flatcall-inlined
benchmarks.axis: the CONTROL for flatcall — identical loop with the leaf function's body written out at the call site

benchmarks.name: mutual
benchmarks.axis: MUTUAL recursion — two functions calling each other, 800 levels deep; the cross-function-call cycle no compiler can inline its way out of

benchmarks.name: tailcall
benchmarks.axis: TAIL-position linear recursion at depth 5_000 — does the runtime eliminate the tail call?
benchmarks.python_scale_why: meta audit: BOTH depth and repeats change; no scalar factor is valid

benchmarks.name: treewalk
benchmarks.axis: recursion over a REAL recursive heap structure — pointer-chasing binary tree, built recursively then walked recursively
benchmarks.python_scale_why: meta audit: dominated by the one-time tree build; a multiply is wrong

benchmarks.name: char-scan
benchmarks.axis: per-character read throughput over a long ASCII string

benchmarks.name: int-format
benchmarks.axis: integer to decimal string, then reading the produced digits back

benchmarks.name: slice-extract
benchmarks.axis: substring extraction: a W-char sliding window materialised at every offset

benchmarks.name: str-eq
benchmarks.axis: string == in a loop: identity-equal / content-equal / early-mismatch / late-mismatch

benchmarks.name: substr-search
benchmarks.axis: indexOf: first occurrence of a 12-char needle in a 1M-char text
benchmarks.python_scale_why: no reduction (str.find is a C routine — interpreter floor does not apply)

benchmarks.name: token-count
benchmarks.axis: tokenising character state machine over a large ASCII text
